Summary

The Second Intifada's immediate trigger was Ariel Sharon's September 28, 2000 visit to the Temple Mount/Haram al-Sharif, accompanied by 1,000 Israeli police. Palestinians viewed this as deliberate provocation at one of Islam's holiest sites by a figure they associated with past massacres (Sabra and Shatila 1982, Qibya 1953). Protests erupted immediately. The next day, September 29 (a Friday), after prayers at Al-Aqsa Mosque, Israeli police fired on Palestinian demonstrators, killing 7 and wounding over 300. By October 1, violence had spread throughout the occupied territories and into Israel. Thirteen Palestinian citizens of Israel were shot dead by Israeli police during protests inside Israel proper. Within two weeks, 100 Palestinians and 10 Israelis had been killed. The uprising's deeper causes lay in the failure of the Oslo peace process: seven years after Oslo, Palestinians remained under occupation, settlements had doubled, movement restrictions had increased, and statehood seemed further away than ever.

Unlike the First Intifada's stones and civil disobedience, the Second Intifada quickly became armed conflict. Palestinian militant groups—Hamas, Islamic Jihad, Al-Aqsa Martyrs' Brigades (affiliated with Fatah), and PFLP—launched devastating suicide bombing campaigns targeting Israeli civilians in buses, restaurants, markets, and nightclubs. The peak came in March 2002 with the Passover massacre at Park Hotel in Netanya (30 killed), triggering Israel's massive Operation Defensive Shield. Israel responded with overwhelming military force: helicopter gunships, F-16 fighter jets, tanks, and bulldozers deployed in densely populated Palestinian areas. Targeted assassinations by helicopter missile strikes often killed bystanders. Entire cities were placed under curfew for months. The 2002 siege of Jenin refugee camp became emblematic: Israeli forces demolished 140+ buildings, killed 52 Palestinians (23 civilians), and faced international accusations of war crimes.

By the Second Intifada's end in late 2005, the toll was catastrophic: 3,223-4,789 Palestinians killed (including 700+ children, 47% civilians); 1,024-1,100 Israelis killed (including 300+ children, 64% civilians); 45,000+ Palestinians wounded; 7,500+ Israelis wounded; approximately 40,000-50,000 Palestinians imprisoned; and massive infrastructure destruction. Israel unilaterally withdrew from Gaza in August 2005 while accelerating settlement expansion in the West Bank. The separation barrier was constructed—declared illegal by the International Court of Justice—confiscating thousands of acres of Palestinian land. The Second Intifada destroyed what remained of the peace process, entrenched the occupation, empowered Hamas, and created the siege of Gaza. It established patterns that continue today: Palestinian resistance met with disproportionate Israeli force; suicide bombings used to justify collective punishment; negotiated peace deemed impossible. The human cost was immense on both sides, but the political outcome was clear: Israeli control deepened while Palestinian freedom receded further.

Timeline

2000-07-01 00:00:00 Camp David peace talks collapseUS President Clinton hosts Israeli PM Ehud Barak and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat at Camp David. Talks fail to reach agreement. Israeli narrative blames Arafat; Palestinian narrative cites inadequate Israeli offers. Failure creates atmosphere of despair and anger among Palestinians. — CFR - Second Intifada Overview
2000-09-28 00:00:00 Trigger: Sharon's Temple Mount visitIsraeli opposition leader Ariel Sharon visits Temple Mount/Haram al-Sharif with 1,000 police. Palestinians view as deliberate provocation at holy site by figure associated with past atrocities. Clashes erupt immediately; Israeli forces kill 4 Palestinians that day, wound dozens. — Britannica - Second Intifada
2000-09-29 00:00:00 Friday prayers massacre: 7 killed, 300+ woundedDay after Sharon's visit, Palestinian worshippers exit Al-Aqsa Mosque after Friday prayers and protest. Israeli police open fire with live ammunition. Kill 7 Palestinians, wound over 300. Violence spreads throughout occupied territories. Second Intifada has begun. — Council on Foreign Relations
2000-09-30 00:00:00 Muhammad al-Durrah killed on camera12-year-old Muhammad al-Durrah shot and killed while cowering with his father behind concrete barrel at Netzarim Junction, Gaza. Death captured on video by France 2 cameraman. Becomes iconic image of Second Intifada. Israeli investigation later claims uncertainty about source of fatal bullets, but footage shows sustained Israeli fire toward the two. — Historical Documentation
2000-10-01 00:00:00 Thirteen Palestinian citizens of Israel killedPalestinian citizens of Israel (inside Israel proper) hold protests in solidarity with occupied territories. Israeli police fire on demonstrators, killing 13 Palestinian citizens of Israel. Or Commission later finds police used excessive force. Event traumatizes Palestinian community inside Israel. — CFR Timeline
2000-10-01 00:00:00 Lynch of two Israeli reservists in RamallahTwo Israeli reserve soldiers accidentally enter Ramallah, taken into Palestinian Authority custody. Mob storms police station, lynches the two soldiers. Brutal killings filmed and broadcast. Provides Israeli justification for targeting PA facilities. Deeply traumatic for Israeli public. — Historical Records
2000-11-09 00:00:00 First Israeli targeted assassinationIsrael assassinates Hussein Abayat, Fatah Tanzim leader, with helicopter missile strike in Bethlehem. Policy of targeted assassinations begins—Israel will kill 232 Palestinians in targeted strikes during Second Intifada, many attacks also killing bystanders. — B'Tselem - Targeted Assassinations
2002-03-27 00:00:00 Passover massacre: 30 killed in Netanya hotelHamas suicide bomber attacks Passover seder at Park Hotel in Netanya. Kills 30 Israelis, wounds 140. Deadliest single attack of Second Intifada. Triggers massive Israeli military response: Operation Defensive Shield. — CFR Timeline
29 March - May 2002 Operation Defensive Shield: largest West Bank operation since 1967Israel launches massive military operation throughout West Bank. Tanks, helicopters, F-16s deployed. Reoccupies Palestinian cities under PA control. Jenin refugee camp siege becomes particularly devastating: 52 Palestinians killed (23 civilians), 140+ buildings demolished. Ramallah under siege; Arafat's compound (Muqata'a) surrounded and partially destroyed. — B'Tselem - Operation Defensive Shield
3-11 April 2002 Siege of Jenin refugee campIsraeli forces besiege Jenin refugee camp. House-to-house fighting. Israel uses armored bulldozers to demolish homes with people inside. 52 Palestinians killed (23 civilians), 23 Israeli soldiers killed. Over 140 buildings demolished. UN fact-finding mission blocked by Israel. International accusations of war crimes. — Human Rights Watch - Jenin Report
2002-2003 Peak of suicide bombing campaignHamas, Islamic Jihad, Al-Aqsa Martyrs' Brigades launch sustained suicide bombing campaign. Attacks on buses, markets, restaurants, nightclubs throughout Israel. Hundreds of Israeli civilians killed. Creates atmosphere of terror in Israeli society. Israel responds with intensified military operations, assassinations, closures. — CFR Documentation
June 2002 - 2005 Separation barrier construction beginsIsrael begins constructing separation barrier—85% inside West Bank (not on Green Line). Stated purpose: prevent suicide bombers. Reality: annexes land, divides Palestinian communities, restricts movement. International Court of Justice rules barrier illegal (2004). Israel continues construction, eventually spanning 700+ km. — B'Tselem - Separation Barrier
2002-07-22 00:00:00 Israeli F-16 strike kills Salah Shehadeh + 14 civiliansIsrael drops one-ton bomb on apartment building in Gaza City to assassinate Hamas military leader Salah Shehadeh. Kills Shehadeh plus 14 civilians including 9 children. Widespread international condemnation. Exemplifies 'collateral damage' from targeted assassination policy. — Human Rights Watch Report
2004-03-22 00:00:00 Israel assassinates Sheikh Ahmed YassinIsraeli helicopter strike kills Hamas founder Sheikh Ahmed Yassin, quadriplegic spiritual leader, as he leaves mosque after dawn prayer. Seven others killed. Massive Palestinian anger. Month later (17 April), Israel assassinates Yassin's successor Abdel Aziz al-Rantisi. Hamas vows revenge. — CFR Timeline
2004-11-11 00:00:00 Yasser Arafat diesPLO Chairman and Palestinian Authority President Yasser Arafat dies in Paris hospital under mysterious circumstances. Had been under Israeli siege in Muqata'a compound for previous two years. Mahmoud Abbas succeeds him. Arafat's death marks end of an era; Second Intifada begins winding down. — Historical Documentation
2005-08-01 00:00:00 Israel's unilateral disengagement from GazaIsrael withdraws 8,500 settlers and military from Gaza Strip. Presented as concession but maintains control of borders, airspace, territorial waters. Disengagement strengthens Israel's hold on West Bank—settlements there accelerate. Gaza becomes 'open-air prison.' Hamas wins Palestinian elections months later (January 2006). — CFR Timeline
2005-02-08 00:00:00 Sharm el-Sheikh Summit: unofficial end of IntifadaIsraeli PM Ariel Sharon and PA President Mahmoud Abbas meet in Egypt. Declare mutual ceasefire. Violence decreases significantly. Generally considered unofficial end of Second Intifada, though no formal declaration. Final toll: 3,200+ Palestinians, 1,000+ Israelis killed over 5 years. — Britannica - Intifada

Testimony

Jamal al-DurrahJamal and his 12-year-old son Muhammad were caught in crossfire at Netzarim Junction, Gaza (30 September 2000). Testified: 'We crouched behind the barrel. I tried to protect my son with my body. The shooting continued for 45 minutes. Muhammad was crying "Father, they're killing me!" Then he was shot and died in my arms.' Their ordeal was filmed. Jamal badly wounded; Muhammad killed. — France 2 television footage; testimony
Anonymous survivor, Jenin refugee campTestified to Human Rights Watch: 'The bulldozers were demolishing homes with people inside. We could hear people screaming. Israeli soldiers wouldn't let us help them. The entire neighborhood was destroyed in a few hours. Bodies were buried under the rubble for days before we could recover them.' — Human Rights Watch - Jenin Report (2002)
Giora BekaSurvived Park Hotel attack (27 March 2002) that killed 30. Testified: 'We were celebrating Passover seder with families. Suddenly there was a massive explosion. Bodies everywhere. Children killed. It was hell. This wasn't war—it was deliberate murder of civilians celebrating a holiday.' — Israeli survivor testimony
Dr. Ahmed ShabaanWorked during siege of Ramallah (2002). Testified to UN: 'Israeli forces imposed total curfew for weeks. Prevented ambulances from reaching patients. We had pregnant women in labor who couldn't reach hospital. People died from treatable conditions because they couldn't get medical care. Entire city was a prison.' — UN human rights documentation
Anonymous Israeli soldierTestimony to Breaking the Silence: 'We were ordered to demolish homes without checking if people were inside. Used bulldozers to create wide paths for tanks—destroyed entire streets. Officers said it was to protect us, but the destruction was far beyond military necessity. Entire families lost everything.' — Breaking the Silence testimonies
Human Rights WatchReport on Jenin (May 2002): 'Israeli forces committed serious violations of international humanitarian law, some amounting prima facie to war crimes... The IDF used armored bulldozers to demolish buildings, in some cases with civilians inside. Israel's refusal to allow an impartial investigation raises concerns about what it is trying to hide.' — Human Rights Watch - Jenin: IDF Military Operations (May 2002)
International Court of JusticeAdvisory Opinion on Wall (9 July 2004): 'The Court finds that the construction of the wall... and its associated régime, are contrary to international law.' Ruled barrier must be dismantled. Found Fourth Geneva Convention applicable. Israel rejected ruling; US vetoed Security Council resolution enforcing it. — ICJ Advisory Opinion (2004)
Kofi AnnanStatement on Second Intifada (October 2000): 'I deplore the excessive use of force by the Israeli authorities. The firing of live ammunition at unarmed demonstrators is totally unjustifiable.' Later (2004) on separation barrier: 'I have consistently said that the wall is illegal under international law.' — UN Secretary-General statements

War crimes

Palestinian Suicide Bombings (War Crimes)Palestinian armed groups (Hamas, Islamic Jihad, Al-Aqsa Martyrs' Brigades) carried out deliberate attacks on Israeli civilians in buses, restaurants, markets, nightclubs. 138 suicide bombings during Second Intifada killed 515 Israeli civilians. Deliberate targeting of civilians constitutes war crimes under international humanitarian law. — Attack Documentation
Targeted Assassinations and Disproportionate ForceIsrael carried out 232 targeted assassinations during Second Intifada. Helicopter missiles and F-16 bombs dropped on densely populated areas killed hundreds of bystanders. July 2002 assassination of Salah Shehadeh killed 14 civilians including 9 children. February 2003 attack on Hamas operative in Gaza killed 11 civilians including 8 children. Disproportionate force violated international humanitarian law. — B'Tselem Documentation
Excessive Destruction in Jenin Refugee CampDuring April 2002 Jenin siege, Israeli forces demolished over 140 buildings, many with people inside. Armored bulldozers destroyed entire neighborhoods. Israel blocked UN fact-finding mission. Human Rights Watch documented 52 Palestinian deaths (23 civilians). International accusations of war crimes. — Human Rights Watch Report
Mass Home DemolitionsIsrael demolished 4,000+ Palestinian homes during Second Intifada—as punishment, for 'military necessity,' or to clear firing zones. Demolished homes of families of suspected attackers without trial. Collective punishment prohibited under Geneva Convention Article 33. Tens of thousands rendered homeless. — B'Tselem Reports
Killing of Children709 Palestinian children and 301 Israeli children killed during Second Intifada. Muhammad al-Durrah (12) became iconic victim—killed while cowering with father under Israeli fire. Many Palestinian children killed by sniper fire, helicopter strikes, or tank shells in residential areas. Failure to protect children and distinguish between combatants and civilians violated international humanitarian law. — Casualty Statistics
Mass Arbitrary Detention40,000-50,000 Palestinians arrested during Second Intifada. Thousands held in administrative detention without charge or trial. Widespread torture documented by human rights organizations. Mass arrests, night raids on homes, detention of minors. Violated rights to liberty, fair trial, and prohibition on torture. — Addameer Documentation
Collective Punishment and ClosureIsrael imposed prolonged curfews on entire Palestinian cities (Nablus under curfew for months). Siege of Ramallah, Bethlehem, other cities cut off food, medicine, electricity. Closure system divided West Bank into isolated cantons. Collective punishment prohibited under Geneva Convention Article 33. — B'Tselem Reports
Separation Barrier (Illegal Under International Law)Israel constructed separation barrier 85% inside West Bank (not on Green Line). International Court of Justice ruled (2004) barrier illegal, constitutes annexation of Palestinian land, must be dismantled. Israel ignored ruling. Barrier divides Palestinian communities, confiscates agricultural land, restricts movement. — ICJ Advisory Opinion

Legal classification

Geneva Conventions - Violations by Both SidesCommon Article 3: Both sides violated prohibition on 'violence to life and person' and 'outrages upon personal dignity.' Palestinian suicide bombings deliberately killed civilians. Israeli forces killed civilians disproportionately.
International Court of Justice - Wall Advisory Opinion (2004)Barrier declared illegal: ICJ ruled separation barrier violates international law because it's built on occupied Palestinian territory. Constitutes de facto annexation.
Principle of Distinction and ProportionalityPalestinian violations: Suicide bombings deliberately targeted civilians—clear violation of principle of distinction between combatants and civilians.
International Humanitarian Law - Occupation ObligationsDuty to protect civilians: As occupying power, Israel had obligation to protect Palestinian civilian population. Prolonged curfews denying access to food and medicine violated this duty.
Geneva Conventions - Violations by Both SidesArticle 33 (Collective Punishment): Israel's home demolitions, prolonged curfews, closures, and siege conditions constituted collective punishment prohibited under Fourth Geneva Convention.
International Court of Justice - Wall Advisory Opinion (2004)Must be dismantled: Court ordered barrier be dismantled and compensation paid. Israel rejected ruling and continued construction.
Principle of Distinction and ProportionalityIsraeli violations: F-16 strikes and helicopter missiles in densely populated areas with high civilian casualties violated principle of proportionality. Military advantage did not justify civilian deaths.
International Humanitarian Law - Occupation ObligationsProhibition on collective punishment: Home demolitions, area closures, and punishment of entire communities for actions of individuals violated absolute prohibition.
Geneva Conventions - Violations by Both SidesArticle 147 (Grave Breaches): Both sides committed grave breaches. Palestinian deliberate targeting of civilians and Israeli 'extensive destruction...not justified by military necessity' constitute war crimes.
International Court of Justice - Wall Advisory Opinion (2004)Fourth Geneva Convention applies: ICJ reaffirmed Fourth Geneva Convention applies to occupied Palestinian territories and Israel must comply.
International Humanitarian Law - Occupation ObligationsProtection of medical personnel: Both sides violated protections for medical personnel and ambulances. Israeli forces fired on ambulances; Palestinian ambulances used to transport militants.

Commanders

1928-2014 Ariel SharonMade provocative Temple Mount visit triggering Second Intifada. As PM, implemented Operation Defensive Shield, targeted assassinations, separation barrier construction, Gaza disengagement. Figure associated with Sabra/Shatila massacre (1982).
1929-2004 Yasser ArafatLed Palestinians during Second Intifada. Israel accused him of directing violence; Palestinians viewed him as under siege. Spent final two years confined to Muqata'a compound. Death in 2004 marked end of era. Controversial legacy.
1935-present Mahmoud Abbas (Abu Mazen)Became PA President after Arafat's death. Negotiated Sharm el-Sheikh ceasefire with Sharon (February 2005) unofficially ending Second Intifada. Continues as PA President, though hasn't held elections since 2006.
1937-2004 (assassinated by Israel) Sheikh Ahmed YassinQuadriplegic spiritual leader of Hamas. Organization carried out numerous suicide bombings during Second Intifada. Assassinated by Israeli helicopter strike after leaving mosque (22 March 2004). Death further radicalized Hamas supporters.
1942-present Ehud BarakPM when Second Intifada erupted. Presided over Camp David talks failure (July 2000). Initial Israeli military response to uprising. Lost election to Sharon (February 2001) due to Intifada violence.
